calls.reason: OpenAI reports mixed accuracy and ORCFLO reports strong repeatability, but neither measures whether users can anticipate individual successes and failures.
Microsoft demonstrates a working SQL and Python integration, but provides no repeated reliability measurements and does not test natural-language output directly driving programs.

Cai and colleagues find substantial gaps in fundamental spatial abilities across eight benchmarks. Despite human-level results on some tasks, these repeated limitations support the claim that GPT-5 lacks general competence across arbitrary tasks.

The AGI Society review finds that published evidence does not establish AGI even for Astra. The packet identifies no validated trustworthy, aligned general AI whose architecture could settle this forecast.
OpenAI documents grammar-constrained tool interfaces, but the packet does not test whether programmers can obtain semantically dependable representations for downstream applications.

The clinical study finds increased adversarial hallucinations, sharply reduced by mitigation; OpenAI reports fewer routine factual errors. This mixed evidence does not establish the broader claim of escalating misinformation risk.
